newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. to vote on Mideast draft; U.S. may veto it.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to vote on Mideast draft; U.S. may veto it.

text.p: The Security Council scheduled a meeting late on Friday to vote on a resolution calling on Israel to rescind a decision to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.

American U.N. envoy Bill Richardson said he opposed the draft, formally submitted by the four European members of the council -- Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden -- and hinted he might veto it, though it was still possible he might cast an abstention.

"The United States has made a good faith effort to reach a consensus on this issue. Regrettably, one member of the council did not even permit a discussion of that alternative option," Richardson told reporters, referring to a proposal for the council to issue an agreed statement rather than vote on a resolution.

Asked whether he would veto the resolution, he said: "I am going back to my mission. I am going to be talking to my government. But you all know the American point of view that the parties themselves should resolve the Middle East issues, and not the council."
A council source said Egypt was the member opposing a council statement, which requires consensus among all 15 members but carries less weight than a resolution.

The council on Thursday completed a two-day debate in which virtually all the nearly 50 speakers criticised Israel's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The site is called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
Arab delegates have said that, in the event of a veto, they would take the issue to the 185-member General Assembly, where there is no veto, though Assembly decisions are not binding.
